005.holdout_note: hold-out is 52 windows but only 5 independent experiments -- sanity check only, NOT a final performance figure. RF hold-out window-level balanced accuracy 0.735 vs experiment-level 0.333 (mean prob) / 0.583 (majority vote): the window figure is inflated by the two long test experiments (No=12 with 22 windows, No=15 with 13 windows carry 35/52 windows), which is exactly the 'window score >> experiment score' warning in 004.
005.conclusion: No improvement over 003. Every LeaveOneGroupOut experiment-level balanced accuracy (0.4375 logreg, 0.4625 / 0.5125 RF) sits inside the group-preserving permutation null (0.406 +/- 0.177, max 0.8125). Increasing rows 16 -> 201 while the number of independent experiments stays 16 did not produce signal.

pairing_effect_14_24.note: Reported CV merges the duplicate pair into one group (17 folds). The naive 18-fold LOO that treats 24 as an independent sample is shown for comparison only. The difference was exactly 0.000 for both models -- predictions were identical on all 18 rows, because 14 and 24 are still predicted correctly when neither is in the training fold. The merge is kept anyway: a zero bias observed after the fact does not make the naive LOO valid.

progress_feature_ablation.note: n_rows, M_sequence_number_{mean,std,max} and proc_frac_* (14 columns) record how far the cut got. 5 of the 8 defective training experiments are machining_finalized == 'no', i.e. runs that STOPPED EARLY, so these columns are a proxy for half the target's own definition. n_rows alone (462-605 rows for unfinalised runs vs 565-2332 for finalised) separates 16/18 training experiments. Dropping the 14 columns barely moves the score, so the same information is also spread across the ordinary sensor statistics.

permutation_check_rf.note: Built separately from the logistic null because a null has to come from the same estimator as the score it judges, and RF is the model that scores highest here. 003/005 only ever built a logistic null.

007.holdout_note: hold-out is 5 experiments (No = 6, 10, 11, 15, 16), looked at exactly once -- sanity check, NOT a final performance figure. Both models predicted [0,0,0,0,1] against y_true [1,1,0,0,1], missing 2 of the 3 defects. RF hold-out ROC AUC 1.0 is not evidence of a perfect model: with 3 positives and 2 negatives a random ranking is perfect with probability 1/10.
007.conclusion: First non-chance score in the project, but it must NOT be reported as defect-prediction performance. RF balanced accuracy 0.8375 beat all 10 group-preserving permutation draws (null 0.463 +/- 0.146, max 0.722), yet 10 permutations bound the empirical p-value at >= 1/11 ~ 0.091, so it is suggestive rather than significant. Logistic 0.725 exactly equals its own null maximum (0.725) and is chance level. Crucially, n_rows ALONE reaches balanced accuracy 0.8375 / ROC AUC 0.8625 -- the same as the best full-feature model -- because unfinalised runs stop early and being unfinalised is half the definition of defect. The models are largely detecting 'this cut was aborted', which is a recording of the outcome rather than a prediction of it.

009.holdout_note: 4 experiments (3 pass / 1 fail), looked at exactly once -- sanity check, NOT a final performance figure. The single failing experiment sets sensitivity to either 0 or 1, and one experiment moves accuracy by 25 percentage points.
009.conclusion: Negative result. With 181 experiment-level features on 13 training experiments (12 CV groups, 9 pass / 4 fail) neither fixed model reaches the majority-class baseline: logistic balanced accuracy 0.458 (empirical p = 0.485 against its own 100-draw group-preserving null) and RF 0.344 (p = 0.634, F1 exactly 0.000 on all 5 seeds -- the forest never predicts a failure). The only configuration above 0.5 is n_rows ALONE (logistic 0.764), which beats every 181-feature model and confirms 008's residual risk 1 -- but its own 1-feature null gives p = 0.109 with the observed score sitting exactly at the null's 95th percentile, so it is not significant either. 008's residual risk 2 (feedrate memorisation) did NOT occur: dropping feedrate changes both scores by exactly 0.000 and feedrate alone scores 0.514 -- though that is because nothing was learned, not because the models are principled. The hold-out is 4/4 correct for both models, and must NOT be read as performance: it contradicts the CV, n = 4 with a single failure, and the one failure it catches (No=9) is the shortest run in the hold-out, so it is indistinguishable from the n_rows shortcut. Raising the permutation count from 007's 10 to 100 was decisive: the null maximum is 0.8375, i.e. shuffled labels reproduce the exact score 007 reported as 'hard to call chance'.
